Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 05: Finding the Cave, Asmat's Trust & Sworn Brotherhood.
Setting: the Wilderness and Cave, the mouth of the Devis' cave beneath stylized faceted rocky cliffs, with ornamental cypress, pomegranate shrubs and sparse vermilion flowers. A modest rocky refuge, not a palace.
Scene: Avtandil and Tariel solemnly clasp hands in an oath of lifelong brotherhood at the cave entrance. Their joined hands are prominent and anatomically clear, their other hands placed over their hearts. Tariel has dark curls and a short dark beard, wearing his signature tawny striped great-cat mantle and fur cap. Avtandil is young and clean-shaven, in a silver-and-gold Eastern helmet, chainmail and vermilion cloak. Asmat stands close beside the two men, with quiet dignity as trusted mediator: young dark-haired woman, charcoal-black hooded dress with a fine gold edge and gentle serious face. The three exchange mutual trust through expressive courtly gestures. A small bronze lamp and a plain earthen water vessel are near the shadowed cave mouth; a simple folded blanket suggests shelter. Exactly three principal figures, all physically together. No hunting brothers, no threatening interrogation, no modern handshake photograph pose. Keep the mood of new friendship after grief.
